name: Sodium lactate

lead: Sodium lactate is a mild salt of lactic acid used in shampoos, liquid soaps and some moisturizers to hold water and balance pH, helping skin feel softer and smoother. It is the salt of lactic acid, a familiar exfoliating acid.

As a humectant it attracts and holds water, and as a salt of a weak acid it buffers pH. It is also a food preservative (E325) and part of hospital fluids such as Ringer's lactate. Its medical roles are better documented than its appearance effects, and no trials were found testing it for appearance.

paras: People meet it as a listed ingredient in everyday cleansers and moisturizers rather than as a product of its own. It is made by fermenting a sugar source and neutralising the resulting lactic acid.

In topical and food use it is generally regarded as low-risk by the sources reviewed. Intravenous use is medical, is contraindicated in lactic acidosis, and can induce panic attacks in people with panic disorder.

angle.text: Sodium lactate helps skin hold water and keeps product pH in range, so skin feels softer and smoother. It is the salt of lactic acid; its medical uses are better documented than its appearance effects.

lead: Sodium lactate is the sodium salt of lactic acid (formula C3H5NaO3), a white powder or colourless liquid with a mild saline taste. It is made by fermenting a sugar source such as corn or beets and neutralising the resulting lactic acid.[1]

It is used as a food additive (E325) acting as preservative, acidity regulator and bulking agent, in shampoos and liquid soaps as a humectant, and in medicine as a component of Ringer's lactate solution.[1][2] It does not contain milk protein.[1]
Its relevance to appearance is as a minor moisturizing and pH-regulating ingredient in personal-care products; no trials were found testing it for appearance.
infobox: Component of Ringer's lactate (WHO Essential Medicines)[1]

paras: In food it serves as a preservative, acidity regulator and bulking agent, and is sold as a liquid or powder.[1] Grokipedia states it is used against Listeria in meat products and is generally recognised as safe by the US FDA; this is AI-generated text.[2]

It is used in shampoos and liquid soaps as a humectant and moisturizer.[1] Grokipedia reports use of up to 10 percent in personal care products at pH of at least 3.5 and a Cosmetic Ingredient Review safety conclusion, which is unverified here.[2]

Sodium lactate is part of Ringer's lactate solution. It has been given intravenously as a bicarbonate source for mild to moderate metabolic acidosis and to treat arrhythmias from overdose of class I antiarrhythmics; it is contraindicated in lactic acidosis.[1] It can induce panic attacks in people with panic disorder and has been used as a diagnostic challenge.[1]

No studies found for cosmetic or appearance use. Registered clinical studies of sodium lactate concern medical questions such as traumatic brain injury,[3] cardiac arrest,[4] heart failure,[5] dengue shock syndrome[6] and depression.[7] Wider lactate-biology research examines exercise acidosis[8] and immune and tumour signalling,[9] which is not about skin.
